title: 10-Year Treasury Note auction (January reopening) — the second reopening of the November benchmark, and the cycle-position control for the December leg
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes, PDF CreationDate 2026-08-04), FlateDecode streams inflated per page and rows rebuilt from Tm coordinates. The page-3 row reads verbatim `10-Year NOTE / R / Thursday, January 07, 2027 / Tuesday, January 12, 2027 / Friday, January 15, 2027`, with the page legend `R --denotes reopening`. 1:00pm ET is Treasury standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2027-01-07 coupon announcement
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-10y-note-2026-12-08 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09), in the same page-by-page read of the schedule PDF that dates that event. THIS IS THAT EVENT OWN DIRECT SUCCESSOR: the January leg is the SECOND reopening of the same security the December leg reopens for the first time — the 2026-11-10 new issue, dated 2026-11-15, maturing 2036-11-15, first coupon 2027-05-15. Filed because the calendar tracks treasury-10y-note-2026-09-09, -10-07 and -11-10 as first-class medium-impact entries, has -12-08 as a proposal, and then stops: the entire January 2027 mid-quarter coupon block is untracked. WHY IT DESERVES ITS OWN LEDGER RATHER THAN A LINE IN THE DECEMBER ONE: it is the cycle-position CONTROL for the December event central size finding. Measured this session from api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov auctions_query (pulled 2026-09-09; 103 of 318 rows are 10-Year TIPS returned as `security_type: Note` and were dropped on a non-null `ref_cpi_on_issue_date`), nominal 10-Year auctions split cleanly by cycle position on the SOMA add-on: NEW issues 35/35 positive since 2018, mean $12.35B, accepted/offering 1.346x; FIRST reopenings (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec) 16/35, mean $0.85B, 1.023x; SECOND reopenings (Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct) 27/35, mean $2.70B, 1.073x — and on the $39B era specifically the second-reopening add-on is 10/10 positive, mean $5.03B, with January the two largest in the series (2025-01-07 $8.57B, 2026-01-12 $11.35B). December and January are the same security at the same size four weeks apart, so they isolate the add-on effect from everything else. EXPECTED SIZE, per the grid rather than any published document: $39B, which would be the 24th consecutive $39B reopening since 2024-03-12 (20 cleared through 2026-07-08 at bid-to-cover mean 2.555, sigma 0.089, range 2.34-2.70). The number becomes published on 2027-01-07. STRUCTURE: the January block runs 3-Year Monday 01-11, 10-Year Tuesday 01-12 and 30-Year WEDNESDAY 01-13 — a compressed Mon/Tue/Wed shape, unlike December Mon/Tue/Thu — all settling Friday 2027-01-15. FOMC PROXIMITY, the December event own question, inverts here: the January 2027 decision is 2027-01-27 (`fomc-2027-01-27`, already tracked), so this leg sits 15 days clear of it rather than inside the meeting. CORRIDOR at the time of filing: `eia-steo-2027-01-12` shares the session; `treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-14`, `opex-2027-01-15`, `fomc-blackout-start-2027-01-16` and `mlk-market-closure-2027-01-18` follow it. NAMED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FILED so a sibling can: the January 3-Year (01-11), the January 30-Year reopening (01-13) and the 2027-01-07 coupon announcement. Proposed as an estimate; symbols: [] and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
